issue: Under § 404(b) of the First Step Act, may a district court reduce the sentence on a noncovered offense that was grouped with a covered crack cocaine offense under the sentencing package doctrine?

sides.position: A district court may reduce a sentence on a noncovered offense grouped with a covered offense, because the First Step Act imposes no extra-textual limit excluding grouped noncovered offenses.
cases: United States v. Hudson, 967 F.3d 605 (7th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Curtis, 66 F.4th 690 (7th Cir. 2023)
United States v. Spencer, 998 F.3d 843 (8th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Richardson, 96 F.4th 659 (4th Cir. 2024)

this_court: Permits the reduction for a grouped noncovered offense, following the Seventh Circuit's reasoning in Hudson. The excerpts do not name the contrary circuits, so the opposing side is not shown.
quote: we agree with the reasoning of the Seventh Circuit that the First Step Act does not exclude noncovered offenses because doing so would impose an "extra-textual limitation" since the statute did not constrain its application to grouped and noncovered offenses.
cite: United States v. Nathaniel Richardson, Jr., 96 F.4th 659 (4th Cir. 2024)
